intro: If you want a stay in central Phayao where you can park for free, walk into town easily, and wake up to breakfast at the hotel's own cafe — M2 Hotel Phayao is a name travellers reach for often, and one that sits near the top of the city's rankings. It's a 28-room, 3-star hotel on Pratu Klong 1 Road, Tambon Wiang, right in the centre. Its draw is a central location, clean rooms, friendly staff and breakfast at Happy Mori Cafe. It's close to Kwan Phayao lake, the bus terminal and the city's restaurants. Rooms start at around ฿700/night — just know the building is starting to show its age and there's no lift, the trade-off for a location and value that guests keep praising.

body.html: M2 Hotel is a small in-town hotel in Phayao that opened around 2015. It sits right in the centre on Pratu Klong 1 Road, Tambon Wiang, not far from Kwan Phayao lake and the bus terminal. The draw isn't designer styling or a long list of facilities — it's a central, easy-to-reach hotel with clean rooms and breakfast at a price budget-minded travellers can manage. On TripAdvisor it has consistently ranked #1 of the hotels in Phayao city, which tells you most guests leave happy.

What reviews mention most is the central location and how friendly the staff are. You're right in town, you can park for free if you drive, and it's a short hop on foot or by car to Kwan Phayao, the restaurants and the city markets. Many guests praise the welcoming reception and how easy check-in is. For travellers visiting Phayao on a modest budget, or using it as a stopover on the way to Chiang Rai or Nan, this kind of location just works.

"Clean room, comfortable bed and really friendly staff who were happy to help. It's right in town so easy to get around, there's free parking and the breakfast has plenty of options. Great value for the price."

The rooms are simple and split between a queen-bed type (Standard Queen) and a twin (Standard Twin). All are air-conditioned with a flat-screen TV, a private hot-water bathroom and free Wi-Fi. Most reviews praise the rooms as clean and tidy, with comfortable beds and a quiet feel, and some have a small balcony. The thing to know is that the building is starting to show its age and there's no lift — if you land an upper-floor room you'll be taking the stairs, which a few guests on the 4th floor found tiring.

On facilities, take it for what it is — a small in-town hotel. There's free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk and breakfast at the in-house Happy Mori Cafe. Breakfast is served à la carte with several options, and more than a few guests quietly rave about the coffee — though it can mean a wait when it's busy. There's no swimming pool and no lift, and parking is limited, so arriving late can make a space harder to find. If you're expecting a resort feel or a lake view from your room, this isn't it — it's a city hotel that does its job well for the money.

On scores, M2 Hotel Phayao sits in the city's strong tier. Averaged across real guest reviews it lands around 8.2 out of 10 — Trip.com gives it about 8.2 from more than 50 reviewers, while TripAdvisor rates it 4.4 out of 5 and ranks it #1 among hotels in Phayao city. The repeated praise is for cleanliness, friendly staff, the central location, value and breakfast. The common gripes are that the building is getting old and there's no lift, a few bathrooms have an awkward layout, parking is limited, and staff cleaning early in the morning can be noisy.

Honestly, this isn't a lakeside boutique or a resort with a view over the water. Its appeal is a central location you can drive to, free parking, breakfast and rooms from around ฿700. A Standard room runs about ฿700 in normal periods and climbs to roughly ฿800–900 over long weekends and holidays. If your trip is about exploring the town, seeing Kwan Phayao, or using Phayao as a base before moving on, it fits the budget nicely. But if you want a lake view from your room or a resort atmosphere, look at the lakeside stays instead.

A tip from reading the reviews closely: if you'd rather not climb stairs, ask for a lower-floor room when you book or at check-in, since there's no lift. Arriving late? Call ahead about parking, as spaces are limited. Breakfast is à la carte, so if you have an early start, order early to avoid the wait. And with only 28 rooms, book ahead for long weekends and holidays — they fill quickly.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — M2 Hotel Phayao

faq.q: Where is M2 Hotel Phayao and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's in central Phayao on Pratu Klong 1 Road, Tambon Wiang, Mueang Phayao, close to Kwan Phayao lake, the bus terminal, Wat Sri Khom Kham and the city's restaurants (about 5–7 minutes by car). There's free parking, so it suits travellers driving themselves or arriving by coach and continuing into town.

faq.q: How much does M2 Hotel Phayao cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around ฿700/night in normal periods. There are 28 rooms, both Standard Twin (two single beds) and Standard Queen (one large bed). Over long weekends and holidays prices rise to roughly ฿800–900. Prices depend on the dates and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is there a lift, parking and breakfast?
faq.a: There's free (but limited) parking, free Wi-Fi and breakfast at the in-house Happy Mori Cafe. However, there's no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs, and there's no swimming pool. Breakfast is served à la carte with several options, and the coffee gets a lot of praise.

faq.q: Is the building old, and how clean is it?
faq.a: The building is starting to show its age (it opened around 2015) and there's no lift, while a few bathrooms have an awkward layout. But on cleanliness, real reviews mostly praise the rooms as clean, tidy, with comfortable beds and a quiet feel — it's well kept for the price, which is why it ranks #1 in the city on TripAdvisor.

faq.q: What's the guest score and who is it best for?
faq.a: The average across real reviews is around 8.2 out of 10 (Trip.com about 8.2 from more than 50 reviewers; TripAdvisor 4.4 out of 5 and ranked #1 among hotels in Phayao city). It's best for travellers who value an in-town location, drivers, and anyone using Phayao as a base who want clean rooms and breakfast at good value. If you want a lake view, a resort feel or a lift, look elsewhere.
